beats.lead: The first message on the early internet was a crash
beats.text: On 29 October 1969, UCLA tried to log in to a computer at SRI over the ARPANET.
beats.note: The machines were an SDS Sigma 7 and an SDS 940.

beats.name: Charley Kline
beats.role: UCLA student programmer. He typed the login command while Bill Duvall waited at SRI.

beats.context: Only "l" and "o" arrived before the SRI machine crashed.

beats.lead: The word was meant to be "login"
beats.text: So the first thing the network ever carried was "lo", as in "lo and behold".
beats.note: The wordplay is a gloss added afterwards, not a plan.

beats.text: About an hour later the machine was adjusted and the full login worked.

beats.line: The internet started with a crash and a retry.
